Let \(H\) be the complement graph. Since \(\Delta(G)\le 5\), every vertex in \(H\) has degree at least \(N-6\), so
\[
|E(H)|\ge \frac{N(N-6)}2.
\]
The condition “among any 7 islands two are connected” means \(G\) has no independent set of size \(7\), so \(H\) has no clique of size \(7\), i.e. \(\omega(H)\le 6\). By Turán’s theorem,
\[
|E(H)|\le \left(1-\frac16\right)\frac{N^2}{2}=\frac{5N^2}{12}.
\]
Thus
\[
\frac{N(N-6)}2 \le \frac{5N^2}{12}
\]
so
\[
6N^2-36N\le 5N^2 \implies N^2-36N\le 0 \implies N\le 36.
\]
This bound is attainable by taking \(G\) as \(6\) disjoint copies of \(K_6\). Then \(\Delta(G)=5\), and any \(7\) vertices contain two in the same \(K_6\), hence connected.

\[
\boxed{36}
\]
